Drizzle generator chose DROP+CREATE for the 7 pre-existing indexes instead of ALTER INDEX RENAME. Acceptable on 84 rows (sub-second rebuild including HNSW), to revisit if applied to a much larger dataset.

First migration apply attempt failed: the autogenerated migration used ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE for memories/skills/context, then created the partial index referencing those values inside the same transaction — PG 17 still forbids that. Splitting into two migration files did not work either because drizzle-kit wraps all pending migrations in a single transaction. Final fix: rebuilt the enum from scratch within a single migration (rename old enum → CREATE new enum with all 5 values → ALTER COLUMN TYPE USING text cast → DROP old enum), allowing the partial index to be created in the same transaction. Schema source unchanged; only the migration SQL diverges from Drizzle's default generator output.

New service vectorize/skills.ts: vectorizeSkillFile (1 call per .md), helper getOrMintSourceId(skillName, skillFile) that does a tuple lookup via metadata->>'skill_name' AND metadata->>'skill_file' and either re-uses the existing source_id or mints Bun.randomUUIDv7(), content_hash via Web Crypto SHA-256 (NOT Bun.hash which is non-cryptographic), short-circuits on hash match — returns {sourceId, created, skipped, chunksProduced}. BUG FIX (chunker.ts): fixed an infinite recursion in recursiveSplit — when sep=='' and parts.length===1 (the body has no remaining separator to break on), the previous condition `if (parts.length === 1 && sep !== '') continue;` skipped the next-separator continue specifically for the empty-string sentinel, dropped into the merge block with parts=[body], and called recursiveSplit(part) on the same body → stack overflow. Removed the `&& sep !== ''` guard so any zero-progress separator falls through to the next one, and the empty-string round naturally drops into the hard-character fallback. Caught by skills/pdf/SKILL.md (15KB, the largest bundled skill); also a latent bug for any future memory/document with monolithic content >2.5KB and no whitespace.

Tests: 7 cases full-pipeline (fresh single-file index, idempotent no-op via content_hash, content change keeps source_id, multi-file same skill = distinct source_ids, CHECK constraint rejects tenant scope on skills via raw SQL + cause-chain message extraction, deleteSkillFileVectors targeted delete, listIndexedSkillFiles discovery)

code_changes: Added gpt-tokenizer@^3.4.0 (pure-JS, 0 deps, MIT) to @fretik/ai dependencies and a `measure:tokens` script in package.json

Created scripts/measure-system-prompt-tokens.ts: standalone Bun script using o200k_base encoder (GPT-4o tokenizer). Measures three surfaces independently — (1) system-prompt.md after HTML-comment stripping (mirrors prompt-renderer.ts:35), (2) every tool's description literal (handles 3 patterns: string literal, [...].join('\n'), and identifier-resolves-to-const) plus its Zod .describe() bodies (tracked separately), (3) each SKILL.md frontmatter description. Reads source files as text and parses with regex — does NOT import the tool factories so no DB/Redis/S3 boot-time side effects. Outputs structured JSON with per-tool, per-skill breakdown plus totals. Wired via `bun run measure:tokens`.

First baseline captured (post-S6, with real tokenizer): system_prompt=10,650 tok, tools_total=6,852 tok (5,821 desc + 1,031 schema describes), skills_catalog=414 tok, grand_total=17,916 tok. The chars/4 estimate from S6 was 12,440 tok on system prompt — o200k_base is ~14% lower, giving a more realistic basis for future delta tracking. The S6 chars/4 baseline (13,841→12,440) stays in global_metrics as historical reference.

PLAN.md Tasks 2/3/4 (tool description compression, system-prompt subsection trims, SKILL.md frontmatter rewrites) DROPPED after honest in-session review (see deviations 1-3). No system-prompt, tool, or SKILL.md content modified in S7. Schema unchanged, no migration.
deviations: TASK 2 DROPPED (tool descriptions compression). After drafting a compressed download-drive-document description (314→~120 tok), the user asked to step back and assess objectively whether the compression was worth it. Honest review: the original tools follow the Claude Code 2026 pattern (When to use / When NOT / Inputs / Output / Constraints sections with concrete file types and modalities). Compressing them strips concrete triggers ('render a chart from a Drive doc', 'vision on scan/PDF for layout/signatures/diagrams', specific output shape, ACL/QUOTA error codes) for ~660 tok of cached prefix at 0.25-0.5× rate — net economic gain ~165-330 tok per turn vs the cost of one mis-routed tool call (5K-10K tok wasted on a wrong tool). ROI negative once the Anthropic April 2026 postmortem context is factored in (verbosity-reducing meta-instructions hurt coding quality and got reverted). Big-4 (python/bash/read/sql-query) confirmed intact. memory.ts already done in S6; rag-search.ts already done in S5-bis. The 6 cibles primaires (download-drive-document, manage-tasks, present-files, vision, list-documents, list-extractions) stay as-is.

TASK 3 DROPPED (system-prompt subsection trims). The Explore agent flagged 7 sub-sections as compressible. Re-reading each one line-by-line: 6/7 of the redundancy claims were FALSE. (a) <sandbox_constraints> 164-170 = pitfalls of persistent kernel (variable shadowing, monkey-patches, NameError after restart) + tool boundary rules (read not cat, bash for ls/grep/find, python for pandas) — all NEW info, not redundant with 147-163. (b) <drive_documents> 211-217 = 5 concrete phrasing→tool-sequence mappings ('Generate Excel from BL' → download + python pandas) — high-signal grounding examples, not bullets-to-table. (c) <domain_tools> 229-232 = the only place the `select:listDocuments` syntax is taught — example IS the teaching. (d) <multi_step> 364-369 = 4 distinct anti-patterns preventing manageTasks over-triggering, not '4 negatives → 1'. (e) <visual_diagrams> 399-405 = 1 Unicode rule + 1 workaround rule (Unicode in labels), not '3× the same rule'. (f) <vague_prompts> 417-420 = step 3 (name your interpretation) and step 4 (offer the runner-up) are complementary actions, not redundant. (g) <file_attachments> vision section 471-488 = 6 concrete patterns of visual questions + 3 anti-patterns + cost anchor — load-bearing teaching examples; only 1-2 marginal cuts possible at best. Net: dropping all 7 cuts. The system prompt is already well-crafted in the Claude Code 2026 idiom; further compression costs precision for ~500 tok of cached prefix that's already at 0.25-0.5× rate.

TASK 4 DROPPED (SKILL.md frontmatter rewrites). Anthropic's official Agent Skills docs specify ~100 tok per skill description as the discovery cost upper bound. Current 8 skills average 52 tok (range 44-65) — already well below the upper bound and shorter than Anthropic's own examples. The Explore agent's suggested rewrites (~33-48 tok each) save ~150-200 tok total (<1% of grand_total) at the cost of stripping concrete signals like 'via matplotlib', 'saved to the sandbox and surfaced inline', 'Platypus vs canvas' etc. Risk of mis-routing on edge cases (wrong skill activated, or skill not activated when relevant) outweighs the marginal cacheable-prefix saving.

Effort vs estimate: 0.5 j PLAN.md → ~0.3 j actual (script + audit + decision). The skipped Tasks 2/3/4 freed time but the audit-then-drop pattern itself was load-bearing — without re-reading the actual content, we'd have shipped compressions that the Anthropic April postmortem explicitly flags as a failure mode (verbosity-reduction instructions hurt quality).

Token measurement script chose o200k_base (GPT-4o encoder) rather than chars/4 per the user's S7 in-flight pivot. Baseline values therefore differ from the S6 chars/4 figures: system_prompt 10,650 tok (o200k_base) vs 12,440 tok (chars/4). Both stored in verification_results for cross-reference. The o200k_base baseline becomes the new reference for any future S7+ comparison since chars/4 is no longer the measurement of record.

deviation_log.summary: Drizzle's autogenerated ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE migration is incompatible with the partial index that filters on the new enum values, even in PG 17. Splitting into two migration files does not help because drizzle-kit wraps all pending migrations in a single transaction. Final approach: rebuild the enum from scratch (rename old → CREATE TYPE new with all 5 values → ALTER COLUMN TYPE USING text cast → DROP old) so all values exist before the partial index references them. This pattern should be the default for any future PLAN session that adds enum values used by partial indexes.

deviation_log.title: skills_global_scope
deviation_log.summary: Cas oublié dans le PLAN initial : les skills sont globaux (pas de team, pas d'org), mais ai_vectors.team_id et ai_vectors.organization_id sont NOT NULL après S1. La proposition initiale du PLAN.md S3 (NIL UUID sentinel '00000000-...') casserait la FK team_id → team.id et est un anti-pattern (sémantique cachée, pas scalable). Décision retenue après revue d'options (NIL UUID / nullable / table dédiée / table ai_skills / skip) : (1) Pas de table ai_skills créée maintenant — skills restent en filesystem bundled (ils sont du code versionné, multi-fichiers dont scripts/*.py, pas des données). Une table ai_team_skills arrivera plus tard pour les skills dynamiques per-team, sans nécessiter de migration sur ai_vectors (juste team_id = X au lieu de NULL). (2) Migration intégrée à S3 : DROP NOT NULL sur team_id et organization_id, ajout d'un CHECK constraint ai_vectors_scope_consistency garantissant '(team_id IS NULL AND organization_id IS NULL) OR (team_id IS NOT NULL AND organization_id IS NOT NULL)', ajout d'un partial index idx_ai_vectors_global ON (source_type) WHERE team_id IS NULL pour le hot path. (3) Source_id stable via lookup : Bun.randomUUIDv7() minté à la première vectorisation, persisté dans ai_vectors lui-même (pas de table de registre). Les re-vectorisations subséquentes ré-utilisent le source_id retrouvé via metadata->>'skill_name'. Garde l'invariant DELETE WHERE (source_type, source_id) du upsert.ts. (4) Vectoriser SKILL.md ET references/*.md. Skip scripts/*.py (code consommé via load_skill() au runtime, pas pour retrieval). (5) S5 hybrid-search.ts : filter étendu à '(team_id = $teamId OR team_id IS NULL)' pour englober les skills globaux, sans NIL UUID.

deviation_log.title: S4_check_constraint_3arm
deviation_log.summary: Cas oublié dans le PLAN initial : le S3 CHECK constraint à 2 bras (skills both NULL / others both set) interdit la forme requise par les context files user-scope (team_id NULL + organization_id NOT NULL + user_id NOT NULL). La parent table ai_context_profiles applique son propre check 'ai_context_profiles_scope_check' qui force team_id NULL pour scope=user — donc le user-scope vector hérite naturellement de team_id NULL. Migration 20260509164228_dusty_tarantula reshape le CHECK à 3 bras : (1) skills AND team_id+organization_id+user_id all NULL ; (2) context AND organization_id NOT NULL (team_id reste optionnel) ; (3) NOT IN (skills, context) AND team_id+organization_id both NOT NULL. Drizzle a généré une migration propre en 1 statement (vs S1 deviation #4 qui exigeait un hand-rewrite à cause du gotcha enum + partial index). Pré-flight : 0 row sur 235 existantes ne viole le nouveau CHECK avant apply. Implication pour S5 : le predicate hybrid-search.ts doit toujours autoriser (team_id IS NULL) pour englober les skills, ET (team_id IS NULL AND user_id = $userId) pour englober les context user-scope. Implication pour futures sessions : ajouter un nouveau source_type force désormais à choisir un des 3 bras (ou créer un 4e), ce qui est le bon endroit pour penser aux conséquences scope. Le prefix tag retenu '[TEAM_CONTEXT]' / '[USER_CONTEXT] file:X' diverge du literal PLAN.md '[CONTEXT_FILE] {filename}' au profit de la symétrie avec [TEAM_MEMORY]/[USER_MEMORY] de S2 — PLAN.md S5 verification step ligne 486 à mettre à jour.
